title: 1961 AHSME Problem 11
statement: Two tangents are drawn to a circle from an exterior point \(A;\) they touch the circle at points \(B\) and \(C,\) respectively. A third tangent intersects segment \(AB\) in \(P\) and \(AC\) in \(R,\) and touches the circle at \(Q.\) If \(AB=20,\) then the perimeter of triangle \(APR\) is:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not determined by the given information

solutions.text:
Equal tangent segments give \(PQ=PB\) and \(RQ=RC.\) Thus \[ \begin{aligned} AP+PR+RA &=AP+PQ\\ &\quad+RQ+RA\\ &=AP+PB\\ &\quad+RC+RA\\ &=AB+AC. \end{aligned} \] Also \(AB=AC=20,\) so the perimeter is \(40.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Tangent segments from the same exterior point have equal lengths
Replace \(PQ\) by \(PB\) and \(RQ\) by \(RC\) in the perimeter
